mia: heads-up: saw a weird one in the generator sample app — ctx cancel doesn't always stop the stream, tokens keep trickling in for ~200ms after cancel.
ben: repro steps?
mia: run the sample with a short deadline, cancel the parent ctx, sometimes generator returns more chunks even after ctx.Err() observed.
priya: do you have logs? could be retry/backoff + auth refresh re-connecting the stream
mia: pasted logs: 
```
2026-11-02T14:22:31.102Z generator: recv chunk id=12
2026-11-02T14:22:31.150Z app: ctx canceled
2026-11-02T14:22:31.301Z generator: recv chunk id=13
```
ben: hmm. that looks like the runtime continued producing after we signaled cancel. is the SDK sending the cancel RPC or just closing locally?
priya: also saw cases where oauth token refresh triggers a short-lived reconnect and the runtime resumes where it left off — combined with local ctx cancel timing that might surface as extra chunks.
mia: here's minimal snippet I used: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Generator().Generate(ctx, req)
for resp.Next() { // streaming
  tok := resp.Recv()
  fmt.Println("tok", tok)
}
```
ben: the SDK should propagate ctx cancellation down to the transport immediately (net.Conn Close). if token-refresh goroutine races with that, you can end up with a small window where in-flight frames are still delivered.
priya: can we add immediate deadline-check before yielding to user callback and drop frames after ctx.Err()? also test-case for generator handshake/resume path.
mia: good idea. in our sample app I tried checking ctx.Err() after each token but still saw 1 extra chunk.
ben: okay both of you: can you try instrumenting the SDK to log when cancel is observed vs when the transport actually closes? that will tell us if transport is late.
priya: will do. also flagged a potential policy bug: if auth refresh happens it may trigger a transparent reconnect that doesn't re-check the original context. i.e., reconnect path should inherit caller ctx or be cancelable.
ben: agreed. reconnect should be bound to the original Generate ctx. otherwise you get "ghost" frames.
infra-bot: deployment note: rolled out 2026-10-29 patch for streaming reconnect backoff (v1.8.2).
mia: repro attached to the thread (+sample app). i can share a small harness.
priya: I pushed a quick change to generator transport to check ctx.Err() immediately after auth refresh and before re-establishing the stream. small unit test added.
ben: nice. add an integration test that cancels mid-handshake and assert no further frames are yielded. can we also add a docs note for sample app about deadlines vs cancellations?
mia: thanks — that will help onboarding; lots of users copy the sample verbatim.
priya: FYI added a TODO to go-sdk backlog: make generator cancel semantics explicit in README and add example patterns (context.WithTimeout vs explicit Cancel func).
ben: once tests green let's cut a minor patch and include in the sample app PR.
mia: :thumbsup:
devex-bot: created issue #1427: "generator: ensure ctx cancellation wins over auth-refresh reconnect" and linked PR draft.
